baslik: How Did the Ottomans Try to Connect the Black Sea & Caspian in 1569? 🗺️ #shorts
aciklama:
As maritime chokepoints face crisis, the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor is reshaping trade between Asia and Europe. Yet 457 years ago, in 1569, the Ottoman Empire tried to open that exact same corridor by digging a canal across the steppe.

Under Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, Ottoman soldiers dug one-third of the Don-Volga trench in August 1569 to sail their fleet into the Caspian Sea. Halted by early winter, Sokollu's visionary canal was completed on the exact same spot 383 years later, in 1952.
